question.value: What is the column density, excitation temperature, and deuteration fraction of di-deuterated methanol (CHD2OH) towards IRAS 16293-2422 A and B using an updated spectroscopic database, and how does its deuteration chain compare to other protostars, laboratory ice experiments, and comets?

evidence.quote: Accurate quantification of the column density of di-deuterated methanol is a key missing puzzle piece in the otherwise thoroughly constrained family of D-bearing methanol in the deeply embedded low-mass protostellar system and astrochemical template source IRAS 16293-2422.

In this paper, new accurate spectroscopic data (Sect. 2.2) are used to firmly quantify the availability of CHD2OH in IRAS 16293-2422 A and B (hereafter, I16293A and I16293B, respectively) on the basis of ALMA-PILS observations

analysis_steps.goal: Construct spectroscopic database and partition function for CHD2OH

method.value: Calculated rotation-torsion energy levels, line frequencies, line strengths using dipole moment components (mu_x = -1.37 D, mu_z = 0.8956 D), and partition function Q_rot-tors from 2.75 to 300 K up to J=26 and frequencies below 500 GHz with an intensity cutoff.

evidence.quote: The results of the global line position analysis of (cite: Coudert2021) were used to build a spectroscopic database for CHD2OH. All rotation-torsion lines within and between the first three torsional states, 0 <= vt <= 2, were computed up to J=26.

Line strengths were evaluated taking a dipole moment function with two non-vanishing constant components along the x and z axes of the molecule-fixed axis system such that the xz plane remains parallel to the COH group. The values are mu_x=-1.37 and mu_z=0.8956 D

key_parameters.value: mu_x = -1.37 D, mu_z = 0.8956 D; frequency < 500 GHz; J <= 26; LOGSTR0 = -9, LOGSTR1 = -9; minimum calculated error = 10 kHz

evidence.quote: The values are mu_x=-1.37 and mu_z=0.8956 D as reported by (cite: Amano1981).
LOGSTR0 and LOGSTR1 are two dimensionless constants both set to -9.
A minimum value of 10 kHz was selected for the calculated error (ERR).

assumptions.value: Vibrational contribution to partition function is negligible (modes > 1000 cm^-1)

evidence.quote: It should be noted that the vibrational contribution to the partition function is negligible, because the vibrational modes are above 1000 cm^-1.

validation.value: Comparison with table 2 of Mukhopadhyay (2016a), identifying 32 transitions with frequency discrepancies > 0.5 MHz caused by past assignment errors.

evidence.quote: A comparison between the present spectroscopic database and a previously available line list is shown in Table [tbl:comp_dtb].

analysis_steps.goal: Filter CHD2OH lines for synthetic spectral fitting

method.value: Constructed an LTE reference spectrum of all known detected species in ALMA-PILS, visually identified and discarded any CHD2OH lines blended with known species, and removed lines predicted to be optically thick (tau > 0.1 at Tex = 50 K or 300 K with N = 1.3 x 10^17 cm^-2), yielding 105 unique lines.

evidence.quote: This check for blending is done through visual inspection; and all lines that have any level of blending are removed from further synthetic spectrum fitting. Then, optically thick lines of CHD2OH are removed from further synthetic spectrum fitting.
After the removal of blended and optically thick lines, 105 unique line frequencies remain that are used for synthetic spectral fitting

key_parameters.value: tau > 0.1 cutoff checked at Tex = 50 K and 300 K with initial column density N = 1.3 x 10^17 cm^-2

evidence.quote: These are assumed to be lines that have tau>0.1 either at Tex=50 or 300 K at N=1.3x10^17 cm^-2 (initial rough estimate of the column density of CHD2OH).

assumptions.value: Local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE) for emission modeling

evidence.quote: The computation is performed under the local thermal equilibrium (LTE) approximation.

validation.value: Overlay reference spectrum on observed data to ensure no blending.

evidence.quote: Next, the observed spectrum is investigated at all covered rest frequencies of CHD2OH lines with the reference spectrum overlaid.

analysis_steps.goal: Derive excitation temperature and column density with MCMC synthetic spectral fitting

method.value: MCMC sampling using EMCEE minimizing a chi-squared like negative log-likelihood across +/- FWHM/2 around all 105 selected line frequencies simultaneously. Two consecutive runs: Run 1 (300 walkers, 250 steps) exploring wide priors, Run 2 (300 walkers, 1000 steps) initiated around best-fit of Run 1. Burn-in of 10% discarded, thinning by 0.3%.

evidence.quote: Finally, synthetic spectral fitting for CHD2OH is carried out with a newly developed routine based on the Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) Python package EMCEE
Two runs of MCMC are executed. The first has 300 walkers for each parameter with each walker taking 250 steps... The second has 300 walkers for each parameter with each taking 1000 steps

key_parameters.value: Source size = 0.5'', beam size = 0.5'', beam-filling factor = 0.5; FWHM = 1.0 km/s (source B) and 2.2 km/s (source A); prior Tex in [50, 400] K, N in [10^13, 10^18] cm^-2

evidence.quote: Several parameters are fixed: beam size of 0.5'', source size of 0.5'', and line full width half-maximum (FWHM) of 1 km s^-1.
specifically: Tex in [50,400] K and N in [10^13,10^18] cm^-2 (the log-prior function is set to infinity outside of these ranges).
All other input parameters are kept the same; only FWHM is changed to 2.2 km s^-1 as deduced from previous analysis of this position

assumptions.value: LTE excitation with single Tex; optical depth correction via Sobolev / LVG approximation beta = (1 - e^-tau)/tau

evidence.quote: The code accounts for optical depth by considering the Sobolev or the large velocity gradient (LVG) approximation: N_up; op. thick = N_up; op. thin x beta, where beta = (1-e^-tau)/tau

fitting.value: EMCEE affine-invariant stretch moves; negative log-likelihood sum over line frequencies and +/- 0.5*FWHM velocity windows

evidence.quote: The walkers undertake the default “stretch moves” of EMCEE (cite: GoodmanWeare2010). The negative likelihood function being minimized is: -1/2 x sum_{nu_line} sum (I_observed - I_model)^2

validation.value: Checked walker convergence, autocorrelation times, mean acceptance fractions (70% for both sources), and inspected corner plots.

evidence.quote: The output of the second MCMC run is checked for convergence and high values of acceptance ratios. For the second MCMC run of the CHD2OH computation, the mean acceptance fraction of the 300 walkers is 70%

findings_qualitative.value: Di-deuterated molecules consistently have higher D/H ratios than their mono-deuterated counterparts in low-mass protostars, indicating successive H-D substitution on grain surfaces rather than changing deuteration environments.

evidence.quote: Di-deuterated molecules consistently have higher D/H ratios than their mono-deuterated counterparts in all low-mass protostars, which may be a natural consequence of H-D substitution reactions as seen in laboratory experiments.

findings_qualitative.value: Deuteration levels in IRAS 16293-2422 are comparable to other low-mass protostars (L483, SVS13-A, NGC 1333-IRAS2A, -IRAS4A, -IRAS4B), refuting the notion that IRAS 16293-2422 is anomalously deuterium-rich.

evidence.quote: Deuteration in IRAS 16293-2422 is not higher than in other low-mass star-forming regions (L483, SVS13-A, NGC 1333-IRAS2A, -IRAS4A, and -IRAS4B).

findings_qualitative.value: The D/H ratios of CHD2OH and HDS in comet 67P/C-G are more than an order of magnitude lower than in IRAS 16293-2422, indicating a warmer natal cloud, lower initial D abundance, or chemical reprocessing for the early Solar System.

evidence.quote: Fig. 6 shows the cometary D/H ratio of D2O, CHD2OH, NH2D, and HDS are significantly (at least one order of magnitude) lower than that in I16293B.

The Solar System’s natal cloud, as traced by comet 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko, may have had a lower initial abundance of D, been warmer than the cloud of IRAS 16293-2422, or been partially reprocessed.

claims.hypothesis: Accurate molecular spectroscopy allows robust determination of CHD2OH column density and excitation temperature towards IRAS 16293-2422 A and B.
claims.experiment: Use a new rotation-torsion spectroscopic database to perform MCMC LTE synthetic spectrum fitting on 105 non-blended, optically thin lines from ALMA-PILS Band 7 data.
claims.finding: CHD2OH is firmly detected in both hot corinos, yielding D/H of 7.7 +/- 1.2% and 7.5 +/- 1.1% in sources B and A, respectively.

evidence.quote: The best-fitting LTE parameters of CHD2OH are N=(1.78+/-0.36)x10^17 cm^-2 and Tex=90.0+/-9 K towards a one-beam offset position from IRAS 16293-2422 B... Towards a (slightly more than) one-beam offset position from IRAS 16293-2422 A... N=(2.22+/-0.44)x10^17 cm^-2 and Tex=127+/-13 K

claims.hypothesis: IRAS 16293-2422 has abnormally elevated deuterium fractionation compared to other low-mass protostars.
claims.experiment: Compare the hot corino D/H ratios of D-bearing molecules in IRAS 16293-2422 to those reported in L483, SVS13-A, and NGC 1333-IRAS2A, -IRAS4A, and -IRAS4B.
claims.result: Systematic differences across early evolutionary Class 0 and I sources are not observed; D/H ratios scatter within similar ranges.
claims.finding: IRAS 16293-2422 is not abnormally deuterium-rich; its larger number of detections reflects observational depth rather than physical anomaly.

evidence.loc: 4.2 Comparison to other low-mass protostars with CHD2OH detections
evidence.quote: However, Fig. 5 does not yield enough evidence to support I16293B being abnormally deuterium-rich among low-mass protostars.

claims.hypothesis: Di-deuterated organic molecules have consistently higher D/H ratios than their mono-deuterated counterparts due to grain-surface H-D substitution reactions.
claims.experiment: Calculate successive deuteration levels in formaldehyde, methanol, methyl formate, dimethyl ether, and methyl cyanide, and compare with laboratory surface-reaction experiments.
claims.result: Fractionation levels of mono-deuterated species entering the second deuteration are 14-25% (mean 20.7 +/- 6.2%), agreeing within uncertainties and matching experimental behaviors where constant D/H flux produces higher multiply deuterated ratios.
claims.finding: Higher deuteration in di-deuterated molecules is a natural outcome of successive H-D substitution rather than fluctuating prestellar deuterium availability.

evidence.quote: Within error bars, all five values agree, implying the same level of deuteration in all di-deuterated species relative to their mono-deuterated variants.
Rather, it seems that this is a natural consequence of H-D substitution reactions on grain-surfaces at cold temperatures.

why_this_data.value: ALMA-PILS provides wide, unbiased Band 7 spectral coverage at high sensitivity and angular resolution (0.5'') resolving the individual hot corinos of A and B while avoiding line confusion limit.

evidence.quote: These data cover the 329-363 GHz frequency range (ALMA Band 7) at a spatial resolution of ~0.5'' (70 au; the applied uniform circular restoring beam). This allows for sources A and B to be studied individually

why_this_method.value: Analyzing a one-beam offset position reduces dust attenuation and optical depth while maintaining high molecular column densities; MCMC simultaneously explores Tex and N across all non-blended optically thin lines.

evidence.quote: This position is favorable for spectral analysis as it displays narrow lines, which reduces blending, and probes the hot dense inner hot corino around source B, while avoiding self-absorption and strong dust absorption on source.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Fitting lines with optical depth tau > 0.1 was rejected because the simple synthetic model does not account for flat-topped profiles of optically thick lines.

evidence.quote: However, it does not properly account for flat-topped line profiles of optically thick lines, therefore being most-suitable for the analysis of optically thin lines.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Rigid-rotor approximation for CHD2OH was rejected due to large amplitude internal rotation of the methyl group.

evidence.quote: Di-deuterated methanol CHD2OH is a non-rigid species displaying a large amplitude internal rotation of its methyl group.

limitations_admitted.value: 0.5'' angular resolution cannot separate binary components A1 and A2 of IRAS 16293-2422 A.

evidence.quote: This allows for sources A and B to be studied individually; however, this is not enough to spatially separate A1 from A2.

limitations_admitted.value: LTE modeling with a single Tex is a simplified model; pessimistic uncertainties of 10% on Tex and 20% on N were adopted.

evidence.quote: However, the model assumptions (e.g., LTE with a single Tex) have much higher uncertainties and so do the data themselves (calibration uncertainty of 5%)... pessimistic errors of 10% and 20% on Tex and N, respectively, are adopted

limitations_admitted.value: Moment 0 maps for source A suffer from line blending and severe velocity gradients.

evidence.quote: Around source A it is still hard to compute an accurate integrated intensity and therefore, the shown map should be interpreted with caution

referee_caveats_inferred: Excitation temperature of CHD2OH (90 K) is noticeably lower than that found for other methanol isotopologs (~300 K); high-excitation lines overpredicted by the 300 K model may be due to remaining spectroscopic errors.
Derivation of column densities of main isotopologs used as denominators often depends on assumed carbon/oxygen isotope ratios or optically thick corrections.
